about: Rows the checker evaluates. Signal kinds: blocker (issue: open = broken), fix (PR: merged = fixed, open = in review), release (owner/repo@tag published = fixed), code (owner/repo:path on the default branch; a regex that means fixed or broken), context (shown, never decides), manual (a dated note with a link). Evidence verified 2026-10-24; rows added and re-verified 2026-10-28; every row re-checked by hand 2026-11-15. A row's optional user block (label, update, caveat, pending + checked, advice) feeds the page's "Can my wallet send after NU7?" answer; added 2026-11-16.

rows.name: Trust Wallet Core
rows.note: Fixed in 4.9.1 (tagged 6 Nov, PR #4934; first GitHub release with it: 4.9.3, 11 Nov): Wallet Core now builds v5 Zcash transactions by default. The app still supplies the branch ID, so apps must update to 4.9.1 or later and pass NU7's 0x77190AD9. Until they do, sends built by older versions are v4, which NU7 rejects. Trust Wallet's own browser extension hadn't updated as of 14 Nov (next row). Vultisig added its own v5 code instead (#6151).

signals.label: v5 is the default transaction version
Grant application for a Wallet Core v5 repair (still open, now fixed upstream)

rows.name: Trust Wallet browser extension
rows.note: Two users reported on #4910 (12 and 14 Nov) that the Chrome extension from the Web Store (26.45.1, 6 Nov) still signs ZEC as v4, so nodes reject transparent sends with "transaction version 4 not supported by the network upgrade Nu7". One reporter found the extension's code isn't built from Wallet Core 4.9.1 or later. A rejected send moves no funds; the ZEC stays in the wallet but can't be sent from the extension until it updates. The extension's source isn't public, so this row rests on those reports; the mobile apps weren't checked.

user.label: Trust Wallet (Chrome extension)
user.update: an extension version built on Wallet Core 4.9.1 or later, which builds v5 transactions (26.45.1, the Web Store version on 14 Nov, still builds v4)
user.advice: Wait for an extension update built on Wallet Core 4.9.1 or later; this row changes when it ships. Trust Wallet's mobile apps weren't checked. If you need to move the ZEC sooner, another wallet that supports transparent ZEC can reach it from the same recovery phrase, but check that it shows your t1 address and balance first.

signals.label: User report: extension 26.45.1 still signs v4
User report: send rejected at broadcast (v4 not supported under NU7)

rows.name: Vultisig: SwapKit ZEC swaps
rows.note: SwapKit builds ZEC swaps as v5 with the NU7 branch ID (read 6 Nov on its Maya, THORChain and Flashnet routes; its NEAR route wasn't tested). Vultisig merged v5 SwapKit signers on 13 Nov (Android #6174, iOS #5685), which also refuse v4 and any branch ID other than the live one. The latest app releases (Android 1.0.124, iOS 1.50.80, both 6 Nov) predate that, so until the next release these swaps still stop with an error before signing and no funds move. Normal sends and THORChain or Maya swaps outside SwapKit moved to v5 earlier in #6151.

user.label: Vultisig (ZEC swaps through SwapKit)
user.update: the first Vultisig release after Android 1.0.124 or iOS 1.50.80
user.pending: The fix merged on 13 Nov (Android #6174, iOS #5685), after the latest app releases (Android 1.0.124 and iOS 1.50.80, both 6 Nov). Until the next release, SwapKit ZEC swaps stop with an error before signing.
user.advice: Wait for the next Vultisig release. Normal ZEC sends, and THORChain or Maya swaps outside SwapKit, already work in the current apps.

signals.label: Closed 6 Nov; #6151 left the SwapKit path unchanged until #6174
v5 for sends and THORChain/Maya swaps, not SwapKit
Cryppit grant request for v5 swap signing (withdrawn 8 Nov)

rows.name: SwapKit: Trezor ZEC signing
rows.note: Trezor signs SwapKit's Zcash sends and swaps as v5, so ZEC received in v6 transactions can be spent. Merged 3 Nov in #216, which carries #189.

rows.name: Zaino (light-wallet indexer)
rows.note: Reported on 1 Nov: Zaino 0.10.1 and 0.10.2 stop at the last block before NU7 with "invalid consensus branch id", reproduced on a Zebra 7.0.0 regtest chain, so Mainnet deployments would stall the same way. The reporter verified that the open PR fixes it, but it isn't merged or released yet.

rows.name: Trezor Suite and Blockbook (ZEC)
rows.note: Blockbook's Zcash config moved to Zebra 7.0.0 for NU7 (#1873, merged 13 Nov), and Suite's fallback branch ID, used only when neither the caller nor Blockbook gives one, is now NU7's 0x77190AD9 (#34308, merged 9 Nov). A Suite release and Trezor's own servers carry these on their own schedule, which can't be seen publicly.

user.label: Trezor Suite (ZEC)
user.caveat: Suite asks the Trezor for v5 transactions and takes the branch ID from Trezor's Blockbook servers. When a Suite release and Trezor's servers carry the NU7 changes can't be seen publicly.

rows.name: Trezor firmware: v4 signing cleanup
rows.note: Trezor plans to stop signing v4 Zcash transactions after NU7 (they become invalid under ZIP 2003). Trezor rates it low priority with no funds at risk: Suite always asks for v5, so only third-party apps that request v4 would get a transaction the network rejects.

user.label: Trezor device in a third-party app
user.advice: With Trezor Suite, pick Trezor Suite instead. A third-party app that still asks the Trezor for a version 4 transaction gets one the network rejects, so ask the app whether it builds v5.

signals.label: Drop v4 signing after NU7 (low priority)

rows.name: Zondax Ledger app (ledger-zcash)
rows.note: No NU7 change found in the repository. Its NU6.3 branch-ID update has been open since 8 Sep. Shielded Ledger work has moved to LedgerHQ/app-zcash and pczt-ledger, which this row doesn't track yet.

rows.name: Noir Wallet
rows.note: v1.0.41 (4 Nov) packages the Zcash wallet for NU7 Mainnet at height 3,543,405. Testnet sends failed on earlier releases; a Free Society Hack team reported a Testnet send working on v1.0.41 the same day. Mainnet and Testnet are separate builds, so users need the right one at 1.0.41 or later.

user.label: Noir Wallet
user.update: Noir 1.0.41 or later (the Mainnet build, not the Testnet one)

rows.name: Zingo (zingolib)
rows.note: Testnet wallets failed with "invalid consensus branch id 0x77190ad9" after Testnet NU7; that was fixed, and zingolib 8.0.0 (29 Oct) moves to the librustzcash NU7 release crates with the Mainnet height. Apps built on zingolib still have to ship their own update.

user.label: Zingo (and apps built on zingolib)
user.update: an app release built on zingolib 8.0.0 or later

rows.name: Zodl Android SDK
rows.note: The SDK's main branch moved to the final NU7 crates (zcash_protocol 0.11.0, which carries the Mainnet height) on 28 Oct, and release 6.0.0 is on Maven Central (published 30 Oct).

signals.label: Main on the final NU7 crates (zcash_protocol 0.11.0)

rows.name: Edge
rows.note: Edge moved off react-native-zcash to its new zcash-native package, on the NU7 zingolib base (merged 4 Nov), and the app moved to it on 5 Nov. Release tag v4.52.3 pins zcash-native 0.1.1, so users are fine once they have that version.

signals.label: Earlier PR, closed in favour of zcash-native

rows.name: Zapp (iOS SDK fork)
rows.note: The open PR signs Testnet transactions with the librustzcash NU7 pre-releases; a Mainnet build is a separate step.

rows.name: WebZjs (MetaMask Snap)
rows.note: The Snap is now maintained by red·dev in red-dev-inc/WebZjs (ChainSafe's repository hasn't changed since April). Its main branch is on the NU6.3 crates (zcash_protocol 0.10), not NU7. The NU7 port is open as #21, next to #27 (NU7 portable keys) and zcash_client_memory #18 (the Ironwood pool). The Snap published on npm (1.0.2, 11 Sep) predates both upgrades, and a user reported in June that shielding is rejected for an incorrect consensus branch ID. Mari of red·dev said on the forum it would be redeployed after NU7.

user.label: MetaMask Zcash Snap (WebZjs)
user.advice: The Snap on npm (1.0.2) predates NU7. Wait for red·dev's NU7 release of the Snap; the ZEC stays at the Snap's addresses meanwhile.

signals.label: Main is on the NU6.3 crates (zcash_protocol 0.10)
User report: shielding rejected for an incorrect consensus branch ID

rows.name: ZNS mint
rows.note: Moved to the final NU7 crates (zcash_protocol 0.11, which carries the Mainnet height) in a PR merged 26 Oct; the older tracking issue was closed on 29 Oct.

rows.name: NEAR Omni Bridge: ZEC
rows.note: The NU7 height is a contract constant. Both contracts are deployed on NEAR with it: zcash-connector.bridge.near reports version 0.9.8, and the code on zcash-client.bridge.near matches the btc-light-client v0.6.1 release byte for byte (checked 30 Oct).

rows.name: THORChain ZEC
rows.note: ZEC is live: on 15 Nov THORNode reported the ZEC chain, signing and trading all unhalted and the pool available. The vault's sends since NU7 are v6 transactions (the latest read was mined in block 3,574,395 on 15 Nov), so they are signed under NU7's rules. The 19 Oct trading halt (an outbound matching bug) was fixed in v3.21.0.

signals.label: Vault send after NU7: v6, block 3,574,395

rows.name: Maya Protocol ZEC
rows.note: ZEC is live: on 15 Nov MAYANode reported the ZEC chain and trading unhalted and the pool available, so the halt after the 19 Aug exploit is over. The vault's sends since NU7 are v5 transactions (the latest read was mined in block 3,574,711 on 15 Nov), so they are signed under NU7's branch ID.

signals.label: Vault send after NU7: v5, block 3,574,711

rows.name: sovright mining-infra
rows.note: NU7 relay clients released on 2 Nov (relay-client-5456ff5), described as the exact binaries deployed in Sovright's four production relay regions, after the final NU7 crates merged on 26 Oct (#128). The pre-activation checklist (#121) is still open with 16 of 27 items unticked, last edited 30 Oct; ingress fixes keep landing (11–14 Nov).

signals.label: NU7 relay clients, deployed in production (2 Nov)
Final NU7 crates pinned for Mainnet
Pre-activation checklist, still open (16 of 27 items unticked)

rows.name: BitGo (wasm-utxo)
rows.note: The NU7 branch ID and Mainnet height are in wasm-utxo (5.15.0 and later), and BitGoJS moved to that version in a PR merged 22 Oct, which also fixed old Zcash recovery defaults.

rows.name: Valar librustzcash fork: early NU7 ID PR
rows.note: A PR to Valar's librustzcash fork proposed exposing NU7 as 0x77190AD8; the final ID is 0x77190AD9. It was closed without merging on 27 Oct and the fork's main branch never carried it, so only code built straight from that PR branch would have the wrong value.

rows.name: librustzcash crates
rows.note: The NU7 Mainnet crate releases are out; wallets built on them still have to ship their own releases.

rows.name: Zebra node
rows.note: Zebra 7.0.0 activates NU7 at 3,543,405. Its end-of-support check (estimated release height 3,526,000 plus 56 days) stops it on Mainnet once the chain passes block 3,684,728, about 17 Dec at 25-second blocks, with warnings after block 3,636,344 (about 3 Dec), so nodes need the next release before then. Zebra 6.4.x stopped itself around 2 Nov.

rows.name: Keystone 3 firmware
rows.note: Works after NU7 as it is: NU7 changes no transaction format or signing algorithm, and the PCZTs Keystone signs carry the target branch ID themselves (str4d, 29 Oct). A PR moving the firmware to the NU7 crates is open anyway.

user.label: Keystone 3
user.caveat: Keystone signs for a companion wallet app, and that app has to be ready for NU7 too: look it up here.

signals.label: str4d: existing firmware will work fine post-NU7

rows.name: KeepKey firmware
rows.note: Firmware 7.16.0 (a pre-release, 28 Oct) signs Ironwood and Orchard-to-Ironwood spends only under the NU6.3 branch ID 0x37A5165B, so it refuses them under NU7's 0x77190AD9. No NU7 change in the repository.

user.label: KeepKey (shielded ZEC)
user.advice: Firmware 7.16.0 signs Ironwood spends only under the old NU6.3 branch ID, so it refuses them now; transparent sends weren't checked. Wait for a KeepKey firmware update, and don't type the device's recovery phrase into a software wallet to get around it.

signals.label: Ironwood signing requires the NU6.3 branch ID

rows.name: Unstoppable Wallet (Android)
rows.note: Moved to Zodl Android SDK 6.0.0, on the final NU7 crates, on 2 Nov on both its master and develop branches. App version 0.53.1 (4 Nov) includes it, so users are fine once they are on 0.53.1 or later. GitHub marks 0.53.1 as a pre-release, and the Play Store version hasn't been checked.

rows.name: Unstoppable Wallet (iOS)
rows.note: Moved to its fork of Zodl Swift SDK 7.0.0 (7.0.0-hs.2) for NU7 in a PR merged 29 Oct, with app version 0.53.1, which the App Store has listed since 2 Nov.

rows.name: Zodl iOS (Swift SDK)
rows.note: Swift SDK 7.0.0 (28 Oct) moves to the final NU7 crates (zcash_protocol 0.11.0), which carry the Mainnet activation height. The Zodl iOS app builds on a private copy of the SDK, but App Store version 3.19.0 (29 Oct) lists NU7 support in its release notes.

user.label: Zodl (iOS app)
user.update: Zodl 3.19.0 or later from the App Store

signals.label: str4d: the app update is in the pipeline

rows.name: Zcash Android and Swift SDKs (original, MIT)
rows.note: 4.0.0 is the final release and support ends at NU7 (ZODL, 22 Oct). Both stay on pre-NU7 librustzcash (zcash_protocol 0.10; the Swift SDK patches in an 7 Aug revision where NU7 has no Mainnet height), so apps still built on them can't send now unless they move to the ZODL SDKs or patch it themselves.

user.label: An app on the original Zcash SDKs (4.0.0 or older)
user.advice: Those SDKs end at NU7, so the app has to move to the ZODL SDKs. Until it does, restore the same recovery phrase in a wallet this board shows as able to send. Only type a recovery phrase into wallet software you trust, downloaded from its official site or app store.

signals.label: Swift SDK on a 7 Aug librustzcash revision
ZODL: end of support for the original SDKs at NU7

rows.name: ShapeShift
rows.note: Fixed in #12825 (merged 6 Nov): Zcash sends had used a fixed NU6.3 branch ID (0x37a5165b), which NU7 nodes reject. Cryppit filed the issue. #12831 (merged 9 Nov) lets the native and Ledger signers spend coins received in a v6 transaction, such as ZEC paid out by NEAR Intents.

user.label: ShapeShift
user.caveat: The fix is in ShapeShift's web app (merged 6 Nov).

signals.label: Merged 9 Nov: spend coins from v6 transactions on native and Ledger

rows.name: Gem Wallet
rows.note: Self-custodial mobile wallet (iOS and Android) with transparent ZEC only, no shielded sends. It builds v5 transactions and takes the consensus branch ID from its own Zebra node, so it moved to NU7's 0x77190AD9 with no code change. On 9 Nov (#1840) its Zcash code moved into its own gem_zcash crate, which takes the branch ID for the next block. A transparent send mined in block 3,543,437, 32 blocks after activation, is a v5 transaction signed under 0x77190AD9 (read from the chain on 8 Nov).

signals.label: Branch ID read from the node, for the next block

rows.name: Konclave (FROST group vault)
rows.note: A group vault for Zcash: members hold FROST shares on their own devices and sign PCZTs that a hosted coordinator builds. Its signing code is on the stable NU7 crates (zcash_protocol 0.11.0) and its upgrade table carries NU7 (0x77190AD9 from block 3,543,405). A real NU7 testnet transaction passes the device's checks in a test. No mainnet NU7 payment checked yet.

user.label: Konclave (group vault)
user.caveat: No Mainnet payment under NU7 has been checked yet.

signals.label: Upgrade table carries the NU7 branch ID
A real NU7 testnet transaction through the device's checks

rows.name: Zallet (zcashd wallet replacement)
rows.note: Moved to the released NU7 crates and Zebra 7.0.0 in a PR merged 30 Oct, and 0.1.0-beta.4 (2 Nov) is the first release with them.

rows.name: Ledger Live
rows.note: Ledger Live's Zcash signer uses device-signer-kit-zcash 0.9.0, which signs Mainnet transparent transactions under the NU7 branch ID from the activation height. It ships in Ledger Live 4.25.0 (desktop and mobile, 22 Oct).

rows.name: Ledger hw-app-btc (JS library)
rows.note: The older hw-app-btc Zcash path picks the branch ID by height and stops at NU6.3, so apps that still sign ZEC through it (ShapeShift patches it) send NU6.3 transactions, which NU7 nodes reject. Ledger Live itself moved to the new signer kit.

signals.label: Issue: NU7 branch ID missing (filed 17 Nov)

rows.name: NEAR omni-transaction-rs
rows.note: NEAR's transaction builder for chain signatures lists Zcash branch IDs up to NU6.3 and has no NU7 entry. Callers can pass a custom ID, so whether an app breaks depends on what it passes.

rows.name: Defuse Labs utxo-lib
rows.note: The UTXO library of NEAR Intents' builders last moved its Zcash branch ID to NU6.3 (18 Aug) and has nothing for NU7. Whether NEAR Intents' ZEC withdrawals still use it is not public.

signals.label: Zcash default branch ID is NU6.3

rows.name: ZelCore utxo-lib
rows.note: ZelCore's UTXO library added NU7's branch ID 0x77190AD9 and the final ZIP 244 signature digest on 7 Nov (PR #9, version 9.39.4). npm still serves 9.37.3 (16 Oct), and whether the ZelCore app has shipped the new version isn't visible.

rows.name: SSP Wallet (Flux)
rows.note: Flux's two-device wallet. SSP Wallet 2.2.2 (10 Nov) builds and signs v5 ZEC transactions (ZIP 225 and ZIP 244), and SSP Key 2.2.3 (10 Nov) co-signs them; the release notes say Zcash sends work again with both apps updated. The relay moved to the NU7 v5 config the same day.

user.label: SSP Wallet (Flux)
user.update: SSP Wallet 2.2.2 and SSP Key 2.2.3 or later (both apps)

rows.name: NozyWallet
rows.note: Orchard and Ironwood wallet built on Zebra. The NU7 branch ID 0x77190AD9 was stamped on 6 Nov (#342) and is in browser extension 2.0.4 (13 Nov). Not tested by us.

rows.name: GLEEC coin config (Komodo DeFi Framework)
rows.note: The ZEC entry in GLEEC's coin list still builds v4 transactions. A pull request moves it to v5 with the NU7 branch ID and 25-second blocks (#2133, open), but it says it needs a Komodo DeFi Framework build with v5 support, and no NU7 branch ID was found in the framework's source on 16 Nov.

signals.label: ZEC to v5 for NU7 (needs a KDF build with v5 support)

rows.name: ZChat (Android)
rows.note: Android Zcash wallet and private messenger. ZChat 2.12.4 and older can't send on Ironwood or NU7: the network rejects their transactions. 2.13.0 (17 Nov) works on NU7; it ships its own build of the official Zcash Android SDK with the NU7 libraries. ZChat says to update in place and never uninstall. Not tested by us.
